Nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$) has an angular $sp^2$-hybridized geometry with an observed $\text{O}-\text{N}-\text{O}$ bond angle of $134^\circ$, which is significantly larger than the ideal $120^\circ$ because a single unshared electron repels the bonding pairs less than a full lone pair does.
III. In solid dinitrogen tetroxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$), the central $\text{N}-\text{N}$ bond distance ($175\text{ pm}$) is exceptionally long compared to a standard hydrazine single bond ($145\text{ pm}$) due to repulsive interactions between occupied $\sigma$ and $\pi$ orbitals across the two planar $\text{NO}_2$ units.
IV. Solid dinitrogen pentoxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$) is diamagnetic and consists of linear $[\text{NO}_2]^+$ cations and planar $[\text{NO}_3]^-$ anions.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) I and III only
B) II, III, and IV only
C) I, II, and IV only
D) I, II, III, and IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Statement I: According to MOT, $\text{NO}$ has $11$ valence electrons. Its configuration is $\sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^*_{2s}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 (\pi^*_{2p_x})^1$. Bond order is $(8 - 3)/2 = 2.5$. The single unpaired electron in $\pi^*_{2p}$ confers paramagnetism. (Statement I is correct).
Step 2: Statement II: In $\text{NO}_2$, the central nitrogen atom has one unpaired electron and two $\sigma$-bonds with resonance-delocalized $\pi$-bonding. Because a single electron exerts less electrostatic repulsion than an electron pair, the two bonding domains open out to $134^\circ$ (larger than normal $120^\circ$). (Statement II is correct).
Step 3: Statement III: In planar $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, the $\text{N}-\text{N}$ bond is remarkably elongated to $175\text{ pm}$ (vs $145\text{ pm}$ in $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$) because of cross-molecule repulsion between bonding pairs and delocalized lone pairs on oxygen atoms, resulting in a weak, easily dissociated $\text{N}-\text{N}$ linkage. (Statement III is correct).
Step 4: Statement IV: Solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is ionic $[\text{NO}_2]^+[\text{NO}_3]^-$, where nitronium $[\text{NO}_2]^+$ is linear ($sp$) and nitrate $[\text{NO}_3]^-$ is trigonal planar ($sp^2$), both species possessing paired electrons and diamagnetism. (Statement IV is correct). Consequently, all four statements (I, II, III, and IV) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Among all the trihalides of nitrogen ($\text{NX}_3$), only nitrogen trifluoride ($\text{NF}_3$) is an exothermic compound ($\Delta_f H^\circ < 0$) and thermally stable, whereas $\text{NCl}_3$, $\text{NBr}_3$, and $\text{NI}_3$ are endothermic and dangerously explosive.
Reason (R): The $\text{N}-\text{F}$ bond enthalpy is exceptionally large because of optimal $2p-2p$ orbital overlap and high bond polarity, which easily compensates for the high dissociation energies of $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{F}_2$; in contrast, $\text{N}-\text{X}$ bonds with heavier halogens are diffuse, weak, and unable to overcome the massive bond dissociation enthalpy of dinitrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A): The standard enthalpy of formation of $\text{NF}_3$ is negative ($\Delta_f H^\circ = -109\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), confirming it is an exothermic and stable compound. In sharp contrast, $\text{NCl}_3$, $\text{NBr}_3$, and $\text{NI}_3$ have positive enthalpies of formation (endothermic) and explode spontaneously upon mechanical shock to yield elemental $\text{N}_2$ and halogens. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R): Synthesis from elements requires breaking the extremely strong triple bond of $\text{N}_2$ ($\Delta_{\text{diss}}H = 941.4\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). For the overall formation to be exothermic, the energy released upon forming three $\text{N}-\text{X}$ bonds must exceed the sum of $\frac{1}{2}\Delta_{\text{diss}}H(\text{N}_2) + \frac{3}{2}\Delta_{\text{diss}}H(\text{X}_2)$. Only fluorine, being small with strong $2p-2p$ overlap and high electronegativity, forms sufficiently strong $\text{N}-\text{F}$ bonds to provide this energetic compensation. For chlorine, bromine, and iodine, larger $np$ orbitals yield weak $\text{N}-\text{X}$ bonds, making $\Delta_f H^\circ > 0$. Thus, Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Reason (R) provides the exact thermodynamic and orbital basis for the stability of $\text{NF}_3$ versus other trihalides. Hence, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Step 4: Distractor analysis: Any assertion denying the exothermic nature of $\text{NF}_3$ or the role of bond dissociation enthalpies contradicts fundamental thermochemical principles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Reactants with Nitric Acid) with List II (Oxidized / Reduced Products Formed):
List I:
A. Solid Iodine ($\text{I}_2$) heated with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$
B. Elemental Sulfur ($\text{S}_8$) heated with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$
C. Copper metal ($\text{Cu}$) treated with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$
D. Zinc metal ($\text{Zn}$) treated with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$

List II:
1. Sulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) and nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$)
2. Iodic acid ($\text{HIO}_3$) and nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$)
3. Cupric nitrate $[\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2]$ and nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$)
4. Zinc nitrate $[\text{Zn(NO}_3)_2]$ and nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A: Hot concentrated nitric acid oxidizes solid iodine to iodic acid ($\text{HIO}_3$):
$\text{I}_2 + 10\text{HNO}_3\text{ (conc.)} \rightarrow 2\text{HIO}_3 + 10\text{NO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hence, A matches with 2.
Step 2: Match B: Hot concentrated nitric acid oxidizes elemental sulfur to sulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$):
$\text{S}_8 + 48\text{HNO}_3\text{ (conc.)} \rightarrow 8\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 48\text{NO}_2 + 16\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hence, B matches with 1.
Step 3: Match C: Copper reacts with dilute nitric acid to yield nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$):
$3\text{Cu} + 8\text{HNO}_3\text{ (dilute)} \rightarrow 3\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hence, C matches with 3.
Step 4: Match D: Zinc reacts with dilute nitric acid to yield nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$):
$4\text{Zn} + 10\text{HNO}_3\text{ (dilute)} \rightarrow 4\text{Zn(NO}_3)_2 + \text{N}_2\text{O} + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hence, D matches with 4.
Therefore, the correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the structural and thermodynamic properties of Group 16 hydrides ($\text{H}_2\text{E}$):
Statement I: The $\text{H}-\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond angles drop precipitously from $\text{H}_2\text{O} (104.5^\circ)$ to $\text{H}_2\text{S} (92.1^\circ)$, $\text{H}_2\text{Se} (91.0^\circ)$, and $\text{H}_2\text{Te} (90.0^\circ)$, indicating that bonding orbitals in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, $\text{H}_2\text{Se}$, and $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ are essentially pure $p$-orbitals with minimal $s-p$ hybridization.
Statement II: The acidic character of Group 16 hydrides in aqueous solution increases in the order $\text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{Te}$ because the decrease in $\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond dissociation enthalpy down the group overwhelmingly outweighs the decrease in electronegativity of the chalcogen atom.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I: In $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, oxygen undergoes significant $sp^3$ hybridization with a bond angle of $104.5^\circ$. However, for sulfur, selenium, and tellurium, the energy gap between the valence $ns$ and $np$ orbitals is larger and electronegativity is lower. Under Drago's rule, little to no hybridization occurs; bonding takes place almost entirely via mutually perpendicular $p$-orbitals (angles near $90^\circ$), while the non-bonding electron pair remains predominantly in the spherical $s$-orbital. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II: Although electronegativity decreases from oxygen ($3.5$) to tellurium ($2.1$), which would predict greater bond polarity in water, the acidic strength is dominated by the ease of heterolytic $\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond cleavage in aqueous solution. The $\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond dissociation enthalpy falls from $463\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $238\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ in $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$. Because bond enthalpy decreases sharply, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ ionizes most readily ($K_a$ is highest), making it the strongest acid. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Since both statements are fully supported by fundamental thermodynamic and structural principles, both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Step 4: Distractor analysis: Assertions claiming that polarity dominates over bond enthalpy in determining acid strength contradict the observed experimental $K_a$ values.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the quantitative estimation of atmospheric ozone ($\text{O}_3$), a gas sample is bubbled through an excess of potassium iodide solution buffered with a borate buffer at $\text{pH} = 9.2$. The liberated iodine is then titrated against standard sodium thiosulfate solution. Based on the stoichiometry of the reactions involved, what is the exact molar relationship between the moles of ozone absorbed and the moles of sodium thiosulfate ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$) consumed at the equivalence point?
options: A) $1\text{ mole of } \text{O}_3 \equiv 4\text{ moles of } \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$
B) $1\text{ mole of } \text{O}_3 \equiv 1\text{ mole of } \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$
C) $2\text{ moles of } \text{O}_3 \equiv 1\text{ mole of } \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$
D) $1\text{ mole of } \text{O}_3 \equiv 2\text{ moles of } \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write the primary reaction between ozone and iodide ions in buffered neutral/alkaline solution:
$\text{O}_3 + 2\text{I}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + \text{I}_2 + 2\text{OH}^-$.
From this reaction, $1\text{ mole of } \text{O}_3$ oxidizes $2\text{ moles of } \text{I}^-$ to generate exactly $1\text{ mole of } \text{I}_2$.
Step 2: Write the redox titration reaction of the liberated iodine with sodium thiosulfate:
$\text{I}_2 + 2\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6 + 2\text{NaI}$.
Here, $1\text{ mole of } \text{I}_2$ consumes exactly $2\text{ moles of } \text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ (thiosulfate).
Step 3: Establish the overall stoichiometric equivalence:
$1\text{ mole of } \text{O}_3 \equiv 1\text{ mole of } \text{I}_2 \equiv 2\text{ moles of } \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$.
Step 4: Distractor analysis: A $1:1$ ratio ignores the two-electron oxidation of two thiosulfate anions to tetrathionate; a $1:4$ ratio mistakenly doubles the equivalents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the structural formulas of peroxodisulfuric acid (Marshall's acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$) and pyrosulfuric acid (oleum, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$). Which of the following analytical statements correctly describes the formal oxidation states of the sulfur atoms and the nature of the oxygen bridging linkages in both acids?
options: A) In $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, both sulfur atoms have an oxidation state of $+6$ with one peroxy bridge ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$); in $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$, both sulfur atoms are in $+6$ with one ether-like bridge ($-\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}-$)
B) In $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, the sulfur atoms have an oxidation state of $+7$ due to eight oxygen atoms; in $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$, sulfur is in $+6$
C) In $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, one sulfur is in $+7$ and the other is in $+5$; in $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$, one sulfur is in $+8$ and the other is in $+4$
D) Both acids possess identical $-\text{O}-\text{O}-$ peroxy linkages with sulfur in differing oxidation states of $+5$ and $+6$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, calculating oxidation number using conventional algebra yields $2(+1) + 2x + 8(-2) = 0 \implies x = +7$. However, sulfur has only 6 valence electrons ($3s^2 3p^4$) and cannot exhibit an oxidation state greater than $+6$.
Step 2: Structural analysis reveals that $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$ contains two peroxy oxygen atoms forming a bridging $-\text{O}-\text{O}-$ linkage. Each peroxy oxygen has an oxidation state of $-1$, while the remaining six oxygen atoms are in the $-2$ oxidation state:
$2(+1) + 2x + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = +6$.
Step 3: In pyrosulfuric acid (oleum, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$), there is no peroxy linkage; instead, the two tetrahedral sulfur centers are linked by a single bridging oxygen atom ($-\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}-$), where all seven oxygen atoms have an oxidation state of $-2$, giving $2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 \implies x = +6$.
Step 4: Distractor analysis: Sulfur cannot possess a $+7$ or $+8$ oxidation state; and oleum contains an oxo bridge rather than a peroxy linkage.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the oxidizing properties and electrode potentials of halogens:
Statement I: Although chlorine has a more negative electron gain enthalpy ($-349\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) than fluorine ($-333\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), fluorine ($E^\circ_{\text{F}_2/\text{F}^-} = +2.87\text{ V}$) is a far more powerful oxidizing agent than chlorine ($E^\circ_{\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-} = +1.36\text{ V}$) in aqueous medium.
Statement II: According to the Born-Haber cycle, the standard electrode potential for the half-reaction $\frac{1}{2}\text{X}_2(\text{g}) + e^- \rightarrow \text{X}^-(\text{aq})$ is determined by the combined enthalpy terms: $\frac{1}{2}\Delta_{\text{diss}}H^\circ + \Delta_{\text{eg}}H^\circ + \Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ$, and the abnormally low bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{F}_2$ alongside the immensely exothermic hydration enthalpy of the small $\text{F}^-$ ion decisively favor fluorine.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I: Fluorine has the highest standard reduction electrode potential ($+2.87\text{ V}$) in the entire periodic table, demonstrating that it oxidizes water to dioxygen instantaneously. Chlorine has $E^\circ = +1.36\text{ V}$. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II: The electrode potential reflects the free energy change of the reduction process in solution, which is governed by three consecutive enthalpy terms via the Born-Haber cycle:
1. Bond dissociation of $\frac{1}{2}\text{X}_2(\text{g})$ (endothermic: $+79.4\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{F}$ vs $+121.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{Cl}$).
2. Electron gain by $\text{X}(\text{g})$ (exothermic: $-333\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{F}$ vs $-349\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{Cl}$).
3. Hydration of $\text{X}^-(\text{g})$ (highly exothermic: $-515\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{F}^-$ vs $-381\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{Cl}^-$).
Step 3: The low bond dissociation energy of $\text{F}_2$ and the extremely large negative hydration enthalpy of the small $\text{F}^-$ ion far outweigh the slight $16\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ deficit in electron gain enthalpy, making $\Delta H^\circ_{\text{total}}$ for fluorine much more negative. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 4: Distractor analysis: Stating that either statement is incorrect ignores the thermodynamic breakdown of the standard electrode potential.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the interhalogen compound iodine heptafluoride ($\text{IF}_7$):
I. According to VSEPR theory, $\text{IF}_7$ possesses a pentagonal bipyramidal geometry resulting from $sp^3d^3$ hybridization of the central iodine atom with zero non-bonding lone pairs.
II. Due to planar steric crowding among the five equatorial fluorine atoms, the equatorial $\text{I}-\text{F}$ bonds ($186\text{ pm}$) are unexpectedly longer than the axial $\text{I}-\text{F}$ bonds ($179\text{ pm}$).
III. $\text{IF}_7$ is the only known interhalogen compound of the $\text{XX}'_7$ stoichiometry because the high ratio between the large atomic radius of iodine and the tiny radius of fluorine is required to coordinate seven ligands without excessive steric repulsion.
IV. Hydrolysis of $\text{IF}_7$ with water yields periodic acid and hydrofluoric acid according to the reaction $\text{IF}_7 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_5\text{IO}_6 + 7\text{HF}$.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) I, II, and III only
B) II, III, and IV only
C) I, II, III, and IV
D) I and IV only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Statement I: In $\text{IF}_7$, iodine has 7 valence electrons, all forming single covalent bonds with seven fluorine atoms. Steric number is 7 (0 lone pairs), yielding $sp^3d^3$ hybridization and a pentagonal bipyramidal molecular geometry. (Statement I is correct).
Step 2: Statement II: In contrast to trigonal bipyramidal molecules (where axial bonds are longer), in pentagonal bipyramidal $\text{IF}_7$, the five equatorial fluorine atoms are crowded closely in a single plane with bond angles of only $72^\circ$. This steric congestion pushes them outward, making equatorial bonds ($186\text{ pm}$) longer than the less-crowded axial bonds ($179\text{ pm}$). (Statement II is correct).
Step 3: Statement III: The ratio of radii $r_{\text{I}} / r_{\text{F}}$ is the highest among all halogen pairs, permitting 7 fluorine atoms to pack around iodine without prohibitive ligand-ligand overlap. (Statement III is correct).
Step 4: Statement IV: Hydrolysis of $\text{IF}_7$ in excess water yields paraperiodic acid ($\text{H}_5\text{IO}_6$) and hydrofluoric acid: $\text{IF}_7 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_5\text{IO}_6 + 7\text{HF}$. (Statement IV is correct). Thus, all statements I, II, III, and IV are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In the gas phase, xenon hexafluoride ($\text{XeF}_6$) does not adopt a regular, centrosymmetric octahedral geometry, but instead exists as a distorted octahedron.
Reason (R): Xenon in $\text{XeF}_6$ possesses 7 electron pairs in its valence shell (6 bonding pairs and 1 non-bonding lone pair), where the stereochemically active lone pair exerts directional repulsion, migrating across faces of the octahedron to produce a fluxional capped octahedral structure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A): Experimental electron diffraction and spectroscopic measurements prove that gaseous $\text{XeF}_6$ lacks an inversion center and does not conform to regular $O_h$ symmetry. Instead, it adopts a distorted octahedral geometry with $C_{3v}$ symmetry. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R): Xenon has 8 valence electrons; in $\text{XeF}_6$, it forms 6 single bonds with fluorine, leaving 1 non-bonding lone pair (steric number 7, $sp^3d^3$ hybridization). According to Gillespie-Nyholm VSEPR theory, this lone pair is stereochemically active and projects out of one triangular face of the octahedron (monocapped octahedron). The lone pair rapidly tunnels between the eight faces of the octahedron, rendering the structure dynamically fluxional. Thus, Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Reason (R) provides the quantum chemical and VSEPR rationale for the geometrical distortion asserted in (A). Hence, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Step 4: Distractor analysis: Claims that the lone pair in $\text{XeF}_6$ is stereochemically inert (like in $[	ext{SeCl}_6]^{2-}$) are incorrect for $\text{XeF}_6$ in the vapor phase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Xenon hexafluoride ($\text{XeF}_6$) cannot be stored or manipulated in silica glass or quartz vessels because it reacts vigorously with silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$) in a stepwise sequence. What are the intermediate xenon oxofluoride and the ultimate explosive xenon oxide formed in this reaction network?
options: A) Xenon tetroxide ($\text{XeO}_4$) as intermediate, culminating in elemental xenon and silicon tetrafluoride
B) Xenon difluoride ($\text{XeF}_2$) as intermediate, culminating in gaseous xenon monoxide ($\text{XeO}$)
C) Xenon oxytetrafluoride ($\text{XeOF}_4$) as the primary intermediate, followed by xenon dioxydifluoride ($\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$), culminating in solid xenon trioxide ($\text{XeO}_3$)
D) Xenon hexachloride ($\text{XeCl}_6$) as intermediate, culminating in silicate complexes
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Xenon hexafluoride is extremely reactive towards oxygen-containing materials, including silica ($\text{SiO}_2$) in glass containers.
Step 2: In the initial stage, $\text{XeF}_6$ attacks silica to produce colourless, volatile liquid xenon oxytetrafluoride and silicon tetrafluoride:
$2\text{XeF}_6 + \text{SiO}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{XeOF}_4 + \text{SiF}_4$.
Step 3: With continued contact, $\text{XeOF}_4$ reacts further with silica to form xenon dioxydifluoride:
$2\text{XeOF}_4 + \text{SiO}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2 + \text{SiF}_4$.
Step 4: Finally, $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ reacts with silica to produce highly explosive xenon trioxide:
$2\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2 + \text{SiO}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{XeO}_3 + \text{SiF}_4$.
Because $\text{XeO}_3$ is violently explosive upon drying, $\text{XeF}_6$ must strictly be handled in apparatus made of nickel or Monel metal, never glass.
Step 5: Distractor analysis: $\text{XeO}$ does not exist as a stable isolable species; $\text{XeO}_4$ requires disproportionation of perxenate salts; and chlorine is completely absent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Fluoride Reaction of Xenon) with List II (Ionic Product Formed & Cation/Anion Geometry):
List I:
A. $\text{XeF}_2 + \text{SbF}_5 \rightarrow$
B. $\text{XeF}_4 + \text{SbF}_5 \rightarrow$
C. $\text{XeF}_6 + \text{KF} \rightarrow$
D. $\text{XeF}_6 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow$

List II:
1. $[\text{XeF}_3]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$ (where $[\text{XeF}_3]^+$ is T-shaped)
2. $[\text{XeF}]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$ (where $[\text{XeF}]^+$ is linear)
3. $\text{XeOF}_4 + 2\text{HF}$ (where $\text{XeOF}_4$ is square pyramidal)
4. $\text{K}^+[\text{XeF}_7]^-$ (where $[\text{XeF}_7]^-$ is capped octahedral / distorted pentagonal bipyramid)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A: $\text{XeF}_2$ transfers a fluoride ion to the strong Lewis acid $\text{SbF}_5$ to form $[\text{XeF}]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$. The diatomic cation $[\text{XeF}]^+$ has a linear geometry. Hence, A matches with 2.
Step 2: Match B: $\text{XeF}_4$ donates a fluoride ion to $\text{SbF}_5$ to form $[\text{XeF}_3]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$. In $[\text{XeF}_3]^+$, xenon has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (steric number 5, $sp^3d$), which gives a T-shaped geometry. Hence, B matches with 1.
Step 3: Match C: $\text{XeF}_6$ accepts a fluoride ion from the alkali metal fluoride donor $\text{KF}$ to produce $\text{K}^+[\text{XeF}_7]^-$. The $[\text{XeF}_7]^-$ ion has 7 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (steric number 8), adopting a capped octahedral geometry. Hence, C matches with 4.
Step 4: Match D: Equimolar partial hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_6$ with water yields $\text{XeOF}_4 + 2\text{HF}$. $\text{XeOF}_4$ has 5 bonding directions and 1 lone pair, adopting a square pyramidal geometry. Hence, D matches with 3.
Therefore, the correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The bleaching action of moist chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$) on vegetable dyestuffs is permanent, whereas the bleaching action of moist sulfur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$) is temporary and reversed upon exposure to air.
Reason (R): Moist chlorine bleaches via oxidation by liberating nascent oxygen ($[\text{O}]$), which irreversibly destroys organic chromophores, whereas moist sulfur dioxide bleaches via reduction by liberating nascent hydrogen ($[\text{H}]$), and the reduced colourless product is re-oxidized back to the original dye by atmospheric dioxygen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A): Bleaching of flowers, fabrics, and dyes with moist chlorine remains permanent upon standing. In contrast, wool, silk, or straw bleached by sulfur dioxide gradually regains its original color when left exposed to ambient air. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R): Chlorine reacts with water to generate hypochlorous acid, which decomposes to liberate nascent oxygen:
$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HCl} + \text{HOCl} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl} + [\text{O}]$.
Nascent oxygen oxidizes the conjugated double bonds in organic chromophores (Coloring Matter $+ [\text{O}] \rightarrow$ Colorless Oxidized Product). This oxidative cleavage is irreversible. In contrast, sulfur dioxide reacts with moisture to release nascent hydrogen:
$\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2[\text{H}]$.
Nascent hydrogen reduces the dye to a colorless leuco form (Coloring Matter $+ 2[\text{H}] \rightarrow$ Colorless Reduced Product). Upon standing in air, atmospheric $\text{O}_2$ oxidizes the leuco compound back to the original conjugated chromophore. Thus, Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Reason (R) provides the definitive chemical explanation for why chlorine bleaching is permanent while sulfur dioxide bleaching is temporary. Hence, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Step 4: Distractor analysis: Stating that chlorine bleaches by reduction or sulfur dioxide by oxidation inverts their fundamental mechanisms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following comprehensive statements regarding the periodic trends and chemical reactivity across Groups 15, 16, 17, and 18 of the p-block:
I. In both Group 15 and Group 16, the boiling point curves of hydrides exhibit a sharp minimum at the second member ($\text{PH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, respectively), because they lack the strong hydrogen bonding present in the first member while possessing smaller van der Waals forces than heavier congeners.
II. The single bond dissociation enthalpies follow the sequence: $\text{C}-\text{C} (348\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) > \text{P}-\text{P} (213\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) > \text{S}-\text{S} (213\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) > \text{N}-\text{N} (160\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) > \text{O}-\text{O} (146\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) > \text{F}-\text{F} (158.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1})$, explaining the pronounced catenation ability of phosphorus and sulfur compared to nitrogen and oxygen.
III. The thermal stability of the highest oxidation state (group valence) diminishes down every p-block group due to the inert pair effect, making $\text{Bi(V)}$, $\text{Pb(IV)}$, and $\text{Tl(III)}$ powerful oxidizing agents.
IV. The fluorinating and oxidizing capacity of xenon binary fluorides decreases in the order $\text{XeF}_6 > \text{XeF}_4 > \text{XeF}_2$, where each is capable of oxidizing lower-valent metal halides to higher fluorides.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) I, II, and III only
B) I, II, III, and IV
C) I, III, and IV only
D) II, III, and IV only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Statement I: In Group 15, boiling points are: $\text{BiH}_3 (290\text{ K}) > \text{SbH}_3 (254\text{ K}) > \text{NH}_3 (238.5\text{ K}) > \text{AsH}_3 (210.6\text{ K}) > \text{PH}_3 (185.5\text{ K})$. The minimum is at $\text{PH}_3$. In Group 16: $\text{H}_2\text{O} (373\text{ K}) > \text{H}_2\text{Te} (269\text{ K}) > \text{H}_2\text{Se} (232\text{ K}) > \text{H}_2\text{S} (213\text{ K})$. The minimum is at $\text{H}_2\text{S}$. (Statement I is correct).
Step 2: Statement II: The compact sizes of nitrogen, oxygen, and fluorine cause intense electrostatic repulsions between non-bonding lone pairs, severely weakening their homonuclear single bonds ($\text{N}-\text{N} = 160$, $\text{O}-\text{O} = 146$, $\text{F}-\text{F} = 158.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$).
